text.p: Ampolex Ltd, now a subsidiary of Mobil Corp, said on Wednesday it had reached a confidential settlement with Ron Brierley's Guinness Peat Group (GPG) Plc over GPG's claims about the conversion rate for Ampolex's convertible notes.

"Ampolex Ltd announced that it has reached agreement with GPG Nominees Pty Ltd (GPG) on a basis for settling the litigation which is currently in progress between the two companies," Ampolex said. "The terms of the settlement have also been agreed to by all parties to the litigation other than Mallesons Stephen Jaques (Mallesons) and the Australian Stock Exchange Ltd (ASX). Ampolex will pursue its claim for damages against Mallesons with as much expedition as the Court allows."
Ampolex said while full terms of the settlement were confidential, it had contributed A$17.9 million and would seek to recover most of this and other damages from Mallesons.

"The sum of A$17.9 million includes a sum which Ampolex has agreed to pay to County (Natwest), GPG and the individuals joined to these proceedings in relation to the Corporations Law claims," Ampolex said.

The dispute centred on a claim by GPG and an associate that the conversion rate for Ampolex convertible notes into ordinary shares should be 6.6-to-1, while the petroleum producer claimed in the New South Wales Supreme Court that the correct conversion rate was 1-for-1. Ampolex said County Natwest and GPG will sell their convertible notes to Mobil Exploration for A$7.00 each and no longer assert a conversion rate other than 1-for-1.

Ampolex, which began the legal challenge in June 1995, said it would ask the court to dismiss its claims against GPG, County and some of their executives and "withdraws those allegations and regrets that they were made".
"Ampolex has written to apologise to these officers and to express regret for any damage to reputation or any distress which may have been caused by the making of such allegations."

Mobil Exploration and Producing Australia Pty Ltd won control of Ampolex with a A$1.36 billion bid in June this year but extended the convertible note offer while the legal challenge continued. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
